title: Land Cruiser 100 Series
verdict: The 100 is the Land Cruiser that went to finishing school: a V8, independent front suspension and a cabin you could take to the opera. The purists sulked, and it turned out to be one of the most durable big wagons on the trail. Budget for the timing belt, though.

paragraphs: In January 1998 Toyota replaced the eight-year-old [[land-cruiser/80-series|80 Series]] with a wagon that broke two Land Cruiser traditions at once. The 100 was the first Land Cruiser with a V8, which Toyota added specifically to sell more trucks in North America, where it was the only engine offered. It was also the first with independent front suspension, chosen along with rack-and-pinion steering to improve on-road handling. Off-roaders grumbled, and they had a point. They also kept buying them.

story.heading: FROM 404T TO 'GRAND CRUISER'
paragraphs: Development started in 1991 under the code name 404T, and the design was frozen in mid-1994. Toyota previewed the truck as the 'Grand Cruiser' at the 32nd Tokyo Motor Show in October 1997. Takeo Kondo is credited as designer, Araco built it in Toyota City, and from 2003 to 2008 it was also assembled in China.

Under one body there were really two trucks. The 100 had a slightly wider chassis, IFS and the new engines. The 105 carried over most of the 80's chassis and drivetrain: coil-sprung solid axles at both ends and straight-six petrol and diesel engines, sold only in Africa, Australia, Russia and South America. You can tell them apart at a glance. The IFS 100 often sits lower at the front, and its wheels are almost flat where the 105's are dished, which lets both keep similar track widths.

story.heading: THE AMERICAN 100
paragraphs: US trucks were all UZJ100s with the 4.7-liter 2UZ-FE V8, rated at 230 hp and 320 lb-ft, driving through an A343F four-speed automatic and an HF2A full-time transfer case. Slee Off-Road notes that, unlike the 80, it has no viscous coupling, just a center differential you can lock. The rear axle is a semi-floating, 32-spline unit with a 9.5-inch ring gear. A rear electric locker was optional only for 1998 and 1999. For 2000 Toyota dropped it, added VSC and A-TRAC traction control, and swapped the weak two-pinion front differential for a four-pinion unit.

The 2003 update was the big one: an A750F five-speed automatic, drive-by-wire throttle, 235 hp, stronger U-joints and fatter driveshafts, 4.10 gears and 17-inch wheels as standard. Late trucks gained VVT-i, and Kelley Blue Book lists 275 hp and 332 lb-ft from 2005. Active Height Control was standard on the [[lexus/lx470|LX 470]] from launch; owners report it also turns up as an option on some Land Cruisers, so check which suspension a given truck has.

story.heading: THE LUXURY TWINS
paragraphs: The 100 was also the basis for the [[lexus/lx470|Lexus LX 470]], sold in Japan as the Toyota Land Cruiser Cygnus. Slee's guide says the Lexus shares the drivetrain but adds body cladding, projector headlights, backlit gauges and standard AHC with adaptive damping from 1998. In 2002 the Cygnus and LX 470 got Night View, which projected an infrared camera image onto the windshield, and they were the first Toyota vehicles with a rollover sensor. In Britain and Ireland the 100 was called the Land Cruiser Amazon. When Toyota marked the Land Cruiser's 50th anniversary in 2000 with commemorative models, global production had reached 3.72 million.

story.heading: HOW IT ENDED
paragraphs: The 100 got a series of small facelifts (lights, grille, spoiler and equipment) and stayed in production until August 2007. The [[land-cruiser/200-series|200 Series]] then kept the formula of V8 power, independent front suspension and a luxury twin in the [[lexus/lx570|LX 570]]. Wikipedia rates the 100 as durable and reliable, with two known weak spots on hard-worked trucks: cracked IFS lower wishbones on trucks that often hit the bump stops, and broken front differentials, mostly on 1998–99 two-pinion units.

Meanwhile, the solid-axle [[land-cruiser/70-series|70 Series]] kept going for buyers who wanted nothing to do with IFS. Today the 100 is a well-documented truck: IH8MUD's 100-series FAQ links to write-ups on everything from the 90,000-mile timing belt to lower ball joints, heater-hose tees and AHC fluid flushes.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE SOLID-AXLE TWIN
callout.title: The 105, and the diesel Australia couldn't forgive
paragraphs: The FZJ105 and HZJ105 looked like 100s but kept the 80's solid axles and straight sixes: the 4.5-liter 1FZ-FE petrol and the 4.2-liter 1HZ diesel. In Australia, the V8 100 was at first sold only in the top GXV trim, while entry and mid-range buyers got the 105.

The trouble was the 1HD-FTE turbo-diesel. It arrived in Australia in October 2000, after being sold in Europe and the UK since 1998, but only with IFS. Australian 4WD Monthly said it plainly: 'We will never forgive Toyota for going independent at the front with the mighty 4.2 turbo-diesel.'

engineering_intro: The 100 has a ladder frame, slightly wider than the 80's, with independent front suspension on torsion bars and rack-and-pinion steering, plus a coil-sprung live rear axle. US trucks use the 4.7-liter 2UZ-FE V8 and a full-time transfer case with a lockable center differential. The wheel pattern changed to 5 on 150 mm with M14 x 1.5 studs.

engineering.note: Slightly wider than the 80's to make room for IFS.
A Land Cruiser first. Ride height is set at the torsion-bar adjusters; rack-and-pinion steering (variable-ratio from 2003).

engineering.v: Live axle on coils, 9.5 in ring gear
engineering.note: Semi-floating, 32-spline shafts, four-pinion diff. 4.30 gears early, 4.10 from 2003.

engineering.v: HF2A full-time with center diff lock
engineering.note: No viscous coupling. VSC and A-TRAC traction control from 2000.
The front diff had two pinions until the 2000 model year, then four.
230 hp at launch, 235 hp from 2003, and 275 hp / 332 lb-ft with VVT-i on late trucks.

generations_table.note: A343F four-speed auto. Rear locker option for 1998–99; 4-pinion front diff, VSC and A-TRAC from 2000.
A750F five-speed auto, drive-by-wire, stronger driveshafts, 4.10 gears, 17-inch wheels.
VVT-i engine; KBB lists 275 hp and 332 lb-ft from the 2005 model year.
IFS only. Europe, the UK and Japan from launch; Australia from October 2000. Not sold in the US.
Solid axles front and rear, carried over from the 80. Africa, Australia, Russia, South America.
AHC and adaptive damping standard from 1998; body cladding and a plusher cabin.

buying_checks.head: Ask for the timing-belt receipt
buying_checks.body: The 2UZ-FE uses a belt, and owners treat the 90,000-mile service (belt, water pump, thermostat, often idlers and seals) as essential. With no paperwork, assume it's due and price it in.

buying_checks.head: Know which front diff you're buying
buying_checks.body: Model-year 1998 and 1999 trucks have the two-pinion front differential that Wikipedia says fails most often under shock loads. The 2000 model year switched to a stronger four-pinion unit, but 1998–99 are also the only years with the optional rear locker.

buying_checks.head: Have the heater-hose tees been done?
buying_checks.body: The plastic tees in the heater hoses get brittle and can crack, dumping coolant. IH8MUD calls them part of the 90k service that most shops, Toyota dealers included, skip.

buying_checks.head: Listen at cold start
buying_checks.body: A tick or pop that sounds like an exhaust leak can be a spark plug working loose. IH8MUD's warning thread says to check the plugs before anything else, because a plug that blows out can take the cylinder-head threads with it.

buying_checks.head: Inspect the IFS
buying_checks.body: Look for cracks in the lower wishbones on trucks that have been driven hard enough to hit the bump stops, and check the lower ball joints and CV boots for play or splits.

buying_checks.head: Try a cold start more than once
buying_checks.body: Slee lists worn starter contacts as a known issue. The symptom is a click with no crank on the first try or two.

buying_checks.head: AHC trucks: check the ride height
buying_checks.body: On an LX 470, or one of the late Land Cruisers with AHC, make sure it levels itself and holds height. Ask when the AHC fluid was last flushed; owners on IH8MUD cite a 60,000-mile interval.

buying_checks.head: Do the body and wiring checks
buying_checks.body: Slee's inspection list applies here too: overspray, filler, frame-straightening marks, a rat's nest of accessory wiring under the dash, and fluids that look neglected. Cracked leather seats are common and costly to re-skin.

repairs.title: Timing belt, water pump and thermostat (the 90k service)
repairs.time: ≈ A long weekend (one owner logged about 15 relaxed hours)
repairs.cost: About $600 in parts for one IH8MUD owner's full kit
repairs.symptoms: No symptoms until it breaks. It's on the service schedule at 90,000 miles, so a truck without receipts is due.
repairs.fix: Drain the coolant, cover the radiator with cardboard, then remove the fan, belts and crank pulley. You'll need a big wrench, a cheater bar and something to hold the crank. Replace the timing belt, tensioner and idlers, the water pump with its gasket and O-ring, the thermostat and gasket, and ideally the cam and crank seals while you're in there. One IH8MUD write-up recommends taking photos and bagging bolts as you go, and finds the factory manual a general guide rather than a step-by-step.
repairs.tools: 3/4-in drive breaker bar and cheater · crank-holding tool · pulley puller · seal puller · thread locker · FIPG gasket maker. IH8MUD parts list (check fitment for your year): water pump 16100-59275-83, timing belt 13568-09070, serpentine belt 90916-02586, thermostat 90916-03100 + gasket 16346-50010, idlers 13503-0F010 / 13505-0F010, crank seal 90311-A0001, cam seals 90311-38065 (x2).

parts.name: Timing belt kit with tensioner, 1998–2007 UZJ100/LX470 (BELTTK021)

repairs.title: Replace the heater-hose pipe tees
repairs.cost: Under $15 in parts; a dealer charges $100–200+
repairs.symptoms: None until a brittle tee cracks and you lose coolant, possibly a long way from home.
repairs.fix: With the engine cold, remove the engine cover and lean in from the side. The tees sit deep in the engine bay, so expect a long reach. Unclip the ground wire attached to the heater hose, work the clamps off with pliers, pull the hoses (soapy water helps), fit new tees and refill the coolant. Replace both, because the hot side fails first.
repairs.tools: Step stool · pliers · flat screwdriver · soapy water · Toyota pipe tee 87248-60460 (x2).

repairs.title: Press in new lower ball joints
repairs.cost: Ball joints plus a 20-ton press if you don't own one
repairs.symptoms: Clunks over bumps, play at the bottom of the knuckle, or simply a high-mileage truck with original joints.
repairs.fix: Support the truck on frame stands, pull the wheels and skid plates, and back the torsion-bar adjusters all the way off. Mark and slide back the torque arms, then remove the lower shock bolt, sway-bar link, cotter pin and ball-joint nut. Break the taper, pull the lower arm, remove the C-clip and press out the old joint (a 2-inch conduit coupler makes a good receiver). Press in the new joint with a 2-inch pipe nipple, refit the clip and reassemble in reverse order, following the factory manual for bolt torques. Reset the torsion bars and get an alignment.
repairs.tools: 20-ton shop press · 22, 19, 14 and 24 mm sockets · snap-ring pliers · sledge or pickle fork · lower ball joint (e.g. Cruiser Outfitters SUS43340) · factory manual section SA-73.

parts.name: Lower ball joint boot kit, 1998–2007 UZJ100/LX470 (SUS100BJ15)

repairs.title: Replace the starter contacts
repairs.time: ≈ 3 hours with experience (one owner's first try took 6.5)
repairs.symptoms: The solenoid clicks but the starter doesn't turn, usually on a cold start, then it fires after two or three tries.
repairs.fix: Disconnect the battery. The starter sits under the intake manifold, so remove the V-bank cover, the intake tube and airbox lid, the accelerator cable and the throttle body, then every hose and the ground strap on the manifold, and lift the manifold off. Photograph everything first. Pull the starter, open the solenoid cover and fit new contacts and a plunger. Moving the wiring-harness bracket out of the way makes the manifold easier to refit. Some owners, like the author of IH8MUD's '90K and starter replacement job' thread, do it during the timing-belt service.
repairs.tools: 10, 12 and 14 mm wrenches and sockets · camera for reference photos · starter contact and plunger kit · new intake gaskets.

parts.name: Starter and solenoid parts catalog, 2002 Land Cruiser 4.7 V8
Valve cover gasket kit, 1998–7/2002 100/LX470 2UZ (VCC2UZKITE) — if the covers come off with the manifold

repairs.title: Flush the AHC fluid
repairs.cost: Toyota AHC fluid; one member priced it at about $30–35 a gallon
repairs.symptoms: Old, dark fluid, a truck that's slow to level, or a lift via the height-sensor links that has left the reservoir low.
repairs.fix: Park on level ground with the suspension in N, engine off. Suck the reservoir empty and refill with fresh AHC fluid. Bleed one corner at a time (front driver, front passenger, rear driver, rear passenger): open the bleeder until that corner bottoms out, close it, start the engine and let the truck re-level, then switch off. Repeat until clean fluid comes out of each bleeder, and never let the reservoir run low.
repairs.tools: 10 mm wrench · clear tube and catch bottle · fluid extractor or turkey baster · Toyota AHC fluid.

repairs.title: Check spark plugs for walking out
repairs.cost: Eight plugs (90080-91180 per the IH8MUD 90k list)
repairs.symptoms: A tick-tick or pop-pop at cold start that sounds like an exhaust leak and, as the plug loosens, doesn't go away when warm. Premature coil-boot and coil failures.
repairs.fix: Pull the coils and check every plug's torque. If one is loose, replace the set and torque them correctly; the thread quotes the factory spec as 13 ft-lb. If the tick is still there afterward, then look for an exhaust leak. A plug that has blown out usually needs a thread insert in the head.
repairs.tools: Spark-plug socket and extension · torque wrench (inch-pound range) · dielectric grease for the coil boots.

parts.name: Spark plug tube seal, 2UZ (VCC50010OEM) — if a valve cover is off

repairs.title: Set the front ride height at the torsion bars
repairs.cost: Free to adjust; new torsion bars cost more
repairs.symptoms: A front end that has settled or sits lower than the rear, or new tires that need more clearance.
repairs.fix: Each torsion bar has an adjuster bolt under the truck, one per side. Turn them evenly and measure both sides, keeping some rake, since IH8MUD members point out the 100 handles best with the rear a little higher. Clean and anti-seize the adjuster threads. If you need real lift or more load capacity, fit uprated torsion bars and matching rear coils, then align.
repairs.tools: Socket and long extension · tape measure · anti-seize · Old Man Emu torsion bars (303001) and rear coils (2865) if upgrading.

parts.name: OME stock/light-load replacement kit with torsion bars (listed as ≈1.5 in lift), 1998–2007 100/LX470 (OME100STKTOR)

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: The 100-series FAQ answer on IH8MUD is 285/75R16 on 16-inch wheels or 285/65R18 on 18s, both about 33 inches. 295/75R16s do fit, with half an inch to an inch of clearance at full turn, but owners call it tight. Even 285/75s can be snug at the rear: one owner measured 3/4 inch to the plastic wheel-well liner.

Every 100 has a center differential you can lock. A rear electric locker was a factory option only for 1998 and 1999. From 2000 Toyota relied on A-TRAC traction control instead, so ARB Air Lockers are the usual retrofit.

faq.q: What's the deal with the 1998–99 front differential?
faq.a: Those years have a two-pinion front diff, and Wikipedia says the pinion could flex away from the ring gear under shock loads. Most reported failures are on 1998–99 trucks. Toyota fitted a four-pinion diff from the 2000 model year, and failures dropped.

faq.q: When is the timing belt due?
faq.a: At the 90,000-mile service. Owners replace the belt, water pump, thermostat and often the idlers, tensioner and cam and crank seals at the same time. IH8MUD has a full parts list and several step-by-step write-ups.

It depends what you want. 2003 and later trucks have the five-speed A750F, stronger driveshafts and 4.10 gears, and late trucks have the 275-hp VVT-i engine. 1998–99 trucks are the only ones with the optional rear locker, but they also have the weaker front diff and, Slee notes, throttle-sensor faults that can stop the truck responding to the pedal.
Kelley Blue Book lists 6,500 lb for 2002–2006 models (5,500 lb for a 1999). From 2003 a bolt-on factory hitch was offered, and the rear crossmember was changed to take it.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: KBB lists 12 mpg city and 15–16 highway, with a 25.4-gallon tank on a 2005. Lifts, 33s and a roof rack make that worse.

The LX 470 had Active Height Control and adaptive damping as standard from 1998, and owners report it was also optional on some Land Cruisers. It works well when maintained. Keep up with fluid flushes (owners cite 60,000 miles), and to lift an AHC truck you can adjust the height-sensor links, as IH8MUD's FAQ covers.

Yes, the 105 (FZJ105 and HZJ105), with coil-sprung solid axles at both ends and straight sixes carried over from the 80. It was never sold in the US; it went to Africa, Australia, Russia and South America.

faq.q: Is the Lexus LX 470 the same truck?
faq.a: Mechanically, yes: same chassis and drivetrain. The [[lexus/lx470|LX 470]] adds body cladding, a plusher cabin and standard AHC with adaptive damping. Slee notes that it often got features before the Land Cruiser did.

The common setup is Old Man Emu: uprated torsion bars up front, matching coils at the rear and new shocks, sold as a kit of about 1.5 inches. The torsion-bar adjusters handle front height. IH8MUD's FAQ also links a thread on Slee's front diff drop, and any height change needs an alignment.

mods.why: Fresh torsion bars, coils and shocks undo years of sag and clear 33s. Getting the front and rear heights to match the truck's load is most of the job.

who.name: Cruiser Outfitters — OME 100 Series kit with torsion bars

mods.why: The factory running boards bend on the first rock, and the IFS front end appreciates a skid plate.
Only 1998–99 trucks offered a factory rear locker. Air lockers add front and rear lockers to the rest.
The stock intake is in the passenger front fender. Slee notes that on US trucks the power antenna has to be swapped for a whip antenna to fit a snorkel.
Pull the third row, fit drawers with a fridge slide and add a bed extension: the same recipe as the 80.
Timing-belt kits, ball joints, wheel bearings and suspension in OEM or OEM-supplier quality.

baseline_service.intro: Assume nothing was done unless there are receipts: on a 100 the big-ticket items are the 90,000-mile timing belt, the drivetrain gear oils that owners skip, and (on LX 470s and any AHC-equipped Land Cruiser) the AHC fluid. Note which transmission you have: 1998–2002 trucks use the A343F four-speed, 2003–07 the A750F five-speed, and Slee says the 2004 update moved to ATF WS and Super Long Life Coolant.

items.spec: SAE 5W-30 · ≈6.8 L with filter (Roughtrax); Amsoil lists 7.2 qt for 2005–07 VVT-i trucks
items.interval: Then per the owner's manual schedule [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: The IH8MUD 90k list gives the dealer filter as 90915-YZZD3 and says a larger JDM filter (90915-20004) is available and preferred by some owners.

items.interval: Inspect at every oil change; replace when dirty
items.note: The cabin filter is easy to forget; IH8MUD's 100-series FAQ links an LX 470/Land Cruiser cabin-filter DIY.

items.interval: Iridiums are due at 120,000 mi, but IH8MUD members do them with the 90k timing belt
items.note: While the coils are out, check every plug for tightness: a tick or pop at cold start can be a plug walking out of the head.

items.item: Timing belt, tensioner, idlers & water pump
items.interval: Every 90,000 mi; a truck with no receipt is due now
items.note: Do the thermostat (90916-03100), cam seals and crank seal while you're in there. IH8MUD members say the cam seals are more work on the 2005–07 VVT-i engine.

parts.name: Timing belt kit w/ tensioner, UZJ100/LX470 (BELTTK021)

items.spec: ≈15 L (Roughtrax). 1998–2003: Toyota red Long Life Coolant · 2004–07: pink Super Long Life Coolant, premixed (Slee)
items.interval: Red LLC every 30,000 mi or 2 years; pink SLLC at 100,000 mi, then every 50,000 mi (Slee)
items.note: Replace the plastic heater-hose tees (87248-60460) preventively; IH8MUD says they go brittle and can dump the coolant. Radiator hoses 16571-50150 / 16572-50150 and the bypass hose are worth doing with the timing belt.

items.interval: Replace with the timing belt, or sooner if cracked or chirping
items.note: The serpentine belt comes off for the timing belt anyway, so replace it and spin-check the idler and tensioner.

items.spec: A343F (1998–2002): Toyota T-IV, ≈2.0 L per drain-and-fill · A750F (2003–07): ≈3.0 L per drain-and-fill, ≈10.6 L dry; ATF WS on trucks without a dipstick (Roughtrax)
items.interval: Then per the owner's manual schedule [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: Slee: from 2004 the dipstick was deleted (level is set at the overflow plug) and ATF WS is not interchangeable with T-IV or Dexron. A drain-and-fill only swaps the sump portion, so repeat it rather than doing one big flush on unknown fluid.

items.spec: GL-5 75W-90 · 1.4 qt (IH8MUD DIY); Roughtrax lists 1.5 L
items.interval: Then per the owner's manual schedule [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: HF2A full-time case, no viscous coupler (Slee). Crack the 24 mm fill plug before the drain, torque the drain plug to 27 ft-lb and don't overtighten: the case can crack. Synthetic can quiet cold-morning whine.

parts.name: Toyota genuine gear oil Super 75W-90 (08885-02106; confirm GL-5 on the label)

items.spec: GL-5 80W-90 hypoid · 1.8 qt (IH8MUD write-up); Roughtrax lists 1.6 L
items.interval: Then per the owner's manual schedule [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: The IFS front diff has Allen-head plugs and too little clearance for squeeze bottles, so bring a pump. Two-pinion on 1998–99, four-pinion from 2000 (Slee).

parts.name: Toyota genuine gear oil Super 75W-90 (08885-02106; confirm GL-5 on the label)

items.spec: GL-5 80W-90 hypoid (LSD-rated per the write-up) · 3.5 qt (IH8MUD); Roughtrax lists 3.2 L, 3.3 L for LSD
items.interval: Then per the owner's manual schedule [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: 9.5-inch ring gear. 1998–99 trucks could have the optional electric rear locker, so test that it engages (Slee).

parts.name: Toyota genuine gear oil Super 75W-90 (08885-02106; confirm GL-5 on the label)

items.spec: Dexron-III ATF (Amsoil lookup) · capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.interval: Refresh by suction-and-refill of the reservoir if dark
items.note: Rack-and-pinion IFS; Slee notes variable-gear steering arrived later in the run.

items.spec: DOT 3 (Amsoil lookup; Roughtrax allows DOT 3 or 4)
items.note: The 100 has a hydraulic brake booster with an electric pump: bleed with the key ON so the pump runs, and expect the ABS and brake lights to come on during the job. IH8MUD members bleed front left, front right, then the rears, and the factory manual describes extra steps for bleeding the actuator.

items.spec: Toyota AHC fluid 08886-01805 (2.5 L can) · ≈4.5 L system, forum estimate (Roughtrax)
items.interval: An IH8MUD member's 2000 owner's manual lists replacement at 60,000 mi
items.note: Never top up with brake fluid; one IH8MUD owner's truck went soft after a dealer did. Bleed each corner with the engine off and the suspension in N.

items.spec: Lithium-base NLGI No. 2 for the U-joints (Roughtrax)
items.note: IH8MUD's FAQ links a driveshaft lubing schematic; any hand grease gun fits the zerks.
